description: The CFG-based taint engine does not fire ReDoS findings on canonical vulnerable patterns when the regex is a literal (no string interpolation). Verified: test/samples/vulnerable_patterns.cr contains Regex.new('(a+)+') and Regex.new('([a-zA-Z]+)*'). CFG engine: 0 findings. Flat engine: 2 findings. Same divergence as the substring-match FP class, but the root cause is different — likely that the CFG engine's transfer_node for ILCall only flags Regex.new when the result is assigned to a tainted LVal (interpolation_tainted path on cfg_taint.ml:~90-100). For a standalone Regex.new literal call, there is no taint flow, so the call never reaches check_call_sinks. Likely fix: in transfer_node for ILCall, when the callee is a known taint-irrelevant sink shape (e.g. Regex.new with a literal arg), still route through check_call_sinks with a synthetic tainted-args=false state so the rule's check_args_contain condition can fire. Verify post-fix: scanning vulnerable_patterns.cr in CFG mode should produce >= 2 ReDoS findings (matching flat engine). Pre-existing gap, not introduced by any prior fix.
title: CFG engine does not detect ReDoS in non-interpolated patterns
